GoBCB feature documentation (English)

0. About this document

Purpose. For every business feature of the GoBCB (rvl-etp) event and ticketing platform, this document shows which screen starts it, which endpoints and services handle it, which queues and workers continue it, which tables, Redis keys and files it touches, which external systems it calls, and where the code is. It is written for RVL's tech lead: an experienced .NET developer who has not worked on a microservices system before. Microservice concepts are explained once, in the platform primer, and every feature links to the explanation it needs.

Who wrote it and from what. It was written from the BS23 delivery side for the handover, from two sources only:

  1. the source code of the five repositories (read-only), at the commits listed under Evidence baseline;
  2. docs/architecture/gobcb-aws-architecture.md for how the platform is hosted on AWS.

The developer test guides (section 11 of each feature) also use the local-development tooling in this workspace (docs/local-dev.md, docs/*-local.md, aspire/, floci/, postman/, scripts/); see Appendix D.

Nothing in this document is invented. Where the code does not answer a question, the text says so and carries a marker [UNCONFIRMED: Q-nn] that links to the question in Open queries. An [UNCONFIRMED] statement is an open question for BS23, not a fact.

How to read a feature

Features are grouped by what starts them: a staff member in the admin portal (A-xx), a customer on the web portal (P-xx) or in the app (U-xx), gate staff in the checker app (C-xx), the system itself on a timer or queue (S-xx), or a concern shared by many features (X-xx, including all authentication and authorization). Each feature is one file with the same eleven sections:

# Section What it answers
1 Name and purpose What the feature is for, in business terms (English and Bangla name)
2 Trigger and actor Who starts it, from which client and screen, with which Cognito pool, role and program scope
3 Business flow The steps as a business user sees them
4 Technical flow The same steps as hops between components; every hop is tagged (see below)
5 Components Clients, services, queues, workers, tables, Redis keys, buckets and external systems involved
6 API contracts Every endpoint the feature uses (method, full path, auth, DTOs, main errors); full JSON samples for the main endpoint(s) only
7 Data and side effects What is written: rows, queue messages, files, emails, pushes, cache entries
8 Code references Where to start reading: controller, manager, worker, client file, with line numbers
9 Handover notes Behaviour that is easy to miss, risks found in the code, and [UNCONFIRMED: Q-nn] items
10 Component relationships A small diagram of this feature only, plus what it depends on and what depends on it
11 Developer test guide How to run it locally: browser, emulator, Postman, Visual Studio debug, and how to verify the result

Hop tags used in section 4:

Tag Meaning
[HTTP + user token] Synchronous HTTP call that carries the caller's Cognito access token (from a client, or forwarded by a service)
[HTTP, no token] Synchronous HTTP call without a token, usually from a background worker to an endpoint that has no [Authorize]
[HTTP, static key] Synchronous HTTP call to an external system with a key from configuration
[SQS: Name] A message put on, or read from, the SQS queue configured as AWS:Queue:Name
[Worker: interval, lock] A background worker in a service, with its hard-coded interval and the Redis lock it takes (if any)
[SignalR] WebSocket message through a SignalR hub
[Shared table] One service reads a table that another service writes (same database, see primer)

Paths. Endpoint paths are written in full as the service exposes them, for example /booking/api/v1/user-booking-order. The first segment is the service prefix (see path-prefix routing).

Corrections to earlier drafts

Two statements in earlier drafts were wrong and have been corrected against the code:

Claim Correction
"The user portal does not call getAllGeneralNotices — it has no caller." It is called and the rows are fetched and filtered; notices is simply never bound in the template (// Fetch notices but do not start the marquee). See P-01 note 2 and A-31 note 2.
"The customer pricing page reads the ticket-pricing content an admin edits." It reads program-pricing (live event prices). getTicketPricingList() has no caller, so nothing published in A-14 is ever shown.
